title: A proper direct image detects a comparison off a finite boundary
statement:
Let $b:Y\to S$ be proper, let $a:G\hookrightarrow Y$ be open
with closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$, and suppose $bi$
is finite.
Let $c:K\to L$ be a morphism of ordinary
bounded-below derived
etale module complexes.
If $a^*c$ and the
direct image $Rb_*c$ are
isomorphisms, then $c$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Fix the commutative coefficient ring $R$ implicit in the statement, and write $U_T$ for forgetting $R$-module sheaves to abelian sheaves. The exact forgetful functor and its derived direct-image comparison are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-direct-image-comparison]. Exactness means that on complexes $U_T$ commutes with kernels, images and quotients, hence $\mathcal H^n(U_TK)=U_T\mathcal H^n(K)$. It reflects isomorphisms of sheaves: the inverse of an invertible underlying abelian sheaf map is $R$-linear because $f(rx)=rf(x)$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology] implies that derived $U_T$ reflects isomorphisms. The inverse-image compatibility of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies $U_Ga^*c$ with $a^{-1}U_Yc$. The natural direct-image comparison identifies $U_SRb_*c$ with $Rb_*U_Yc$. Both are isomorphisms by the hypotheses. It suffices to prove that $\bar c=U_Yc$ is an isomorphism in $D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}})$; from now until the final step all complexes and sheaves are abelian, without changing sites or assuming torsion.

proof.text: Choose a distinguished cone triangle $U_YK\xrightarrow{\bar c}U_YL\to M\to U_YK[1]$ in the bounded-below derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] induces a triangulated termwise functor by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]; $Rb_*$ is triangulated by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]. Apply each functor to this triangle. In either resulting triangle the first arrow is an isomorphism by step 1. Its long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] has isomorphisms at both $\mathcal H^n$ and $\mathcal H^{n+1}$ of the first arrow. Exactness therefore forces the cohomology of the third term to vanish in every degree. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology] to the unique morphism from zero proves $a^{-1}M=0$ and $Rb_*M=0$.

The closed immersion $i$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], so $i_*$ is exact and $Ri_*=i_*$ on $D^+$ by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]. Also $i^{-1}$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact]. Their termwise functors and the adjunction unit of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] therefore descend to complexes and to the derived category. For every $n$, set $F=\mathcal H^n(M)$. Exactness gives $a^{-1}F=\mathcal H^n(a^{-1}M)=0$. At a geometric point in $G$, [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] identifies the stalk of this restriction with the stalk of $F$, so $F$ is supported on $Z$. By [lem-kun-04ca], $F\simeq i_*H$ for some abelian sheaf $H$, and the counit $i^{-1}i_*H\to H$ is invertible. The adjunction triangle identity $i_*\varepsilon_H\circ\eta_{i_*H}=1$ then makes $\eta_{i_*H}$ the inverse of $i_*\varepsilon_H$; for an isomorphism $\theta:F\to i_*H$, naturality gives $\eta_F=(i_*i^{-1}\theta)^{-1}\circ\eta_{i_*H}\circ\theta$, a composite of isomorphisms. Consequently the complex unit $\eta_M:M\to i_*i^{-1}M$ induces the isomorphism $\eta_F:F\to i_*i^{-1}F$ on each cohomology sheaf, since both functors are exact. It is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology]. This proves $M\simeq Ri_*i^{-1}M$ without assuming constructibility, finite coefficients, or quasi-compactness of $a$.

Put $N=i^{-1}M\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}})$. Apply $Rb_*$ to the isomorphism of step 3. Composition of derived direct images [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] gives $Rb_*Ri_*N\simeq R(bi)_*N$. Here the sites are the chosen small representatives of the small etale sites, the ring sheaves are the constant integer sheaves, and the inverse images are those of scheme morphisms, exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact]. Thus these are morphisms of ringed topoi satisfying the cited theorem. Its unbounded comparison restricts to $D^+$: bounded-below injective representatives are K-injective and compute the functors there by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Combining with $Rb_*M=0$ from step 2 yields $R(bi)_*N=0$. Since $bi$ is finite by hypothesis, [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] computes this functor termwise, so $(bi)_*\mathcal H^n(N)=\mathcal H^n(R(bi)_*N)=0$ for every $n$; exactness commutes with the kernel/image quotient defining cohomology.

proof.text: Fix $n$ and write $H=\mathcal H^n(N)$. For any geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z$, let $\bar s=(bi)\bar z$. By [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula], the zero group $((bi)_*H)_{\bar s}$ is the finite product of stalks $H_{\bar z'}$ in the geometric fibre, including $H_{\bar z}$. Inclusion of a factor by zero in all other factors followed by projection is its identity. Therefore each factor, in particular $H_{\bar z}$, is zero. The morphism $0\to H$ is an isomorphism on every geometric stalk, hence an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. This proves $\mathcal H^n(N)=0$ for every $n$. The empty-fibre product causes no problem: no $\bar z$ lies in an empty fibre.

By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology], the cohomology vanishing in step 5 implies $N=0$. The isomorphism $M\simeq i_*N$ from step 3 implies $M=0$. Apply the long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] to the original cone triangle: its zero third term makes every $\mathcal H^n(\bar c)$ an isomorphism. The cohomology criterion [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology] gives that $\bar c$ is an isomorphism. The reflection argument of step 1 gives that the original module morphism $c$ is an isomorphism. Properness of $b$ remains a hypothesis of the item but is not needed for this detection argument.
